scopes.name: anon.public.health
scopes.description: Public health-check endpoint. Liveness signal — no auth.

scopes.name: anon.auth.signin.attempt
scopes.description: Anonymous sign-in attempt — issuing an authentication request before a session exists.

scopes.name: self.read
scopes.description: Read the caller's own user data (profile, preferences, contact details).

scopes.name: self.write
scopes.description: Write the caller's own non-auth-relevant data (display name, avatar, preferences). Auth-relevant changes (email, password) require sensitive scopes.

scopes.name: auth.password.change
scopes.description: Change the caller's own password. Self-service.

scopes.name: auth.user.impersonate.consent
scopes.description: Initiate consent-based impersonation of another user. Requires OTP authorization from the target user.

scopes.name: auth.user.impersonate.force
scopes.description: Initiate force impersonation (no consent — silent). Admin-org-only fallback for emergency support scenarios.

scopes.name: billing.payment.charge
scopes.description: Initiate a payment charge against a customer's billing instrument.

scopes.name: internal.kc.sign
scopes.description: Sign a payload with a KeyCustodian-managed signing key (internal service-to-service / in-process minter).

scopes.name: internal.kc.keyring
scopes.description: Fetch a payload-encryption keyring from KeyCustodian (internal service-to-service / in-process). The scope gates whether a caller may reach the keyring surface at all; a per-workload domain policy decides which domains it may fetch.

scopes.name: internal.kc.issue
scopes.description: Request a workload leaf certificate from KeyCustodian by submitting a certificate-signing request (internal service-to-service, cross-process only). The scope gates whether a caller may reach the issuance surface at all; the leaf subject-alternative-name is always the authenticated mTLS peer identity, never caller-supplied.

scopes.name: internal.kc.cacert
scopes.description: Fetch the certificate-authority chain (root + issuing intermediate) from KeyCustodian (internal service-to-service / in-process). Public trust-anchor material distributed over already-trusted internal channels only.
